preview_text: Argentina beat Algeria 3-0 in Round 1 as Lionel Messi scored a hat-trick — goals in the 17th (assist Rodrigo De Paul), 60th, and 76th (assist Nicolas Gonzalez) minutes. Nahuel Molina replaced Gonzalo Montiel at halftime. A dominant opening performance from the defending champions.

Lionel Messi leads the Argentina projection at 21.72 fpts as the confirmed corner kick taker at $11,400 — he scored three times in Round 1. Julian Alvarez (14.04 fpts, $8,200) replaced Lautaro Martinez in the 55th minute of Round 1 and starts here. Enzo Fernandez (12.12 fpts, $7,200) anchors the midfield.

Argentina project 1.92 goals against Austria's 0.76. Nahuel Molina (9.79 fpts, 20.88% proj_own) in defense entered at halftime in Round 1 and starts here. Rodrigo De Paul (10.10 fpts, $5,900, confirmed corner kick taker) assisted Messi's first Round 1 goal from midfield.

Argentina stack construction centers on Messi with Alvarez and De Paul as the two additional corner-taking pieces. Thiago Almada (11.27 fpts, $6,200) was replaced by a substitute in Round 1 at 55 minutes but starts here and provides a differentiation option. Alexis Mac Allister (9.56 fpts, $5,000) offers a deeper midfield value play.

Austria beat Jordan 3-1 in Round 1 — Romano Schmid scored in the 21st minute and Marko Arnautovic entered at halftime, going on to score a penalty in injury time. Arnautovic starts here in place of Sasa Kalajdzic as the confirmed lineup change from Round 1.

Marcel Sabitzer leads the Austria projection at 12.27 fpts in attack as the confirmed corner kick taker at $7,800. Romano Schmid (10.04 fpts, $6,600) scored the Round 1 opener and carries that form forward. Marko Arnautovic (9.80 fpts, $7,000) scored in Round 1 as a substitute and now starts for the first time this tournament.

Austria project 0.76 goals against Argentina's 1.92 as significant underdogs. Phillipp Mwene (7.49 fpts, 11.27% proj_own) was substituted off at 59 minutes in Round 1 — he starts here and brings attacking width from defense. Konrad Laimer (7.41 fpts, $3,800) in midfield is the low-salary value option.

Austria GPP plays require a competitive game script against the defending champions. Sabitzer and Schmid form the stack core, with Arnautovic providing the third attacking piece after his Round 1 impact from the bench. Kevin Danso (4.91 fpts, 6.30% proj_own) in defense at $2,700 offers a deeply-owned salary-floor option.

France beat Senegal 3-1 in Round 1 — Mbappe scored twice (66th and 90+6th minutes, the opener assisted by Michael Olise), and Bradley Barcola scored in the 82nd minute after entering for Dembele at 80 minutes. Lucas Digne was not in the Round 1 starting lineup — he replaces Theo Hernandez at left back here for Round 2.

Kylian Mbappe leads the France projection at 22.35 fpts in attack at $10,800 — he scored twice in Round 1. Michael Olise (22.14 fpts, $9,800, confirmed corner kick taker) assisted the opening goal and is the highest-owned player on this slate at 47.06% proj_own. Ousmane Dembele (18.00 fpts, $9,200) provides the third major attacking piece.

France project 3.07 goals against Iraq's 0.43 — the most lopsided matchup on this slate at 88.68% implied win probability. Lucas Digne (11.61 fpts, 35.13% proj_own) in defense replaces Theo Hernandez and carries very high ownership as a confirmed wide defender with attacking upside. Bradley Barcola (14.23 fpts, $8,300) scored in Round 1 as a substitute and now enters the starting lineup.

France's stack is exceptionally deep against the most lopsided matchup on this slate — Mbappe, Olise, and Dembele all project over 18 fpts. Barcola at $8,300 offers the most attractive differentiation angle after scoring in Round 1. Jules Kounde (10.21 fpts, $5,000) provides the value anchor in defense.

Iraq lost 4-1 to Norway in Round 1 — Ayman Hussein scored their lone goal in the 39th minute (assist Amir Al Ammari) before conceding twice to the Norway center forward and further goals from a substitute and a late own goal. Iqbal entered for Zaid Ismail at 59 minutes and starts here.

Merchas Doski leads the Iraq projection at 7.88 fpts in defense at $4,300. Amir Al Ammari (6.79 fpts, $3,600) is the confirmed corner kick taker — he assisted Iraq's lone Round 1 goal. Iqbal (4.85 fpts, $4,600) starts after entering as a substitute at 59 minutes in Round 1.

Iraq project 0.43 goals against France's 3.07. At 3.31% implied win probability, Iraq plays are pure tournament-minimum GPP. Jalal Hassan (4.48 fpts, 4.31% proj_own) in goal at $3,600 will likely face exceptional shot volume given France's projected output.

Iraq GPP plays are salary-floor leverage against the heaviest favorite on this slate. Al Ammari as the confirmed corner taker at $3,600 and Doski in defense at $4,300 form the Iraq two-player core. Hussein (3.95 fpts, $5,200) carries the highest salary on the Iraq roster but the lowest proj_own at 0.50%.

Norway beat Iraq 4-1 in Round 1 — Erling Haaland scored twice (29th and 43rd minutes, the opener assisted by David Moller Wolfe), Leo Ostigard added a third in the 76th minute after entering as a substitute, and Iraq conceded a late own goal. A dominant attacking display that now faces a more competitive matchup against Senegal.

Erling Haaland leads the Norway projection at 16.93 fpts in attack at $10,600 — he scored twice in Round 1. Martin Odegaard (12.96 fpts, $8,400) is the confirmed corner kick taker in midfield. Antonio Nusa (12.57 fpts, $8,000) and Alexander Sorloth (12.07 fpts, $7,600) provide the supporting attacking output in a game Norway are favored to win but face more resistance than Round 1.

Norway project 1.47 goals against Senegal's 1.18 — the tightest total on this slate at 2.64. Julian Ryerson (11.78 fpts, 14.25% proj_own) in defense is the confirmed second corner kick taker at $6,800 — a consistent attacking right-sided defender who played the full 90 in Round 1.

Norway's stack is built around Haaland with Odegaard and Nusa as the natural complements. Ryerson at 14.25% proj_own offers the value differentiation play from the likely-heavy Haaland exposure. David Moller Wolfe (7.42 fpts, 2.32% proj_own) assisted the opening Round 1 goal and is the lowest-owned viable Norway option.

Senegal lost 3-1 to France in Round 1 — a late substitute scored a consolation goal in stoppage time. Habib Diarra replaced Lamine Camara at 76 minutes, and Iliman Ndiaye replaced Pape Gueye at 83 minutes. A defeat that puts real pressure on this Round 2 matchup against a Norway side fresh off a 4-1 win.

Ismaila Sarr leads the Senegal projection at 9.48 fpts in attack at $5,500. El Hadji Malick Diouf (8.56 fpts, 16.57% proj_own) in defense is a confirmed corner kick taker. Krepin Diatta (7.32 fpts, $4,100) in defense is the second confirmed corner kick taker. Lamine Camara (8.49 fpts, $5,300) provides midfield output between the two set-piece defenders.

Senegal project 1.18 goals against Norway's 1.47 in the most competitive game on this slate at 27.72% implied draw probability. Nicolas Jackson (7.85 fpts, 2.98% proj_own) in attack at $5,700 offers a deeply-owned option as the primary center forward. Edouard Mendy (6.34 fpts, 17.56% proj_own) in goal carries significant ownership for a goalkeeper.

Senegal GPP plays leverage the competitive nature of this matchup — the 27.72% draw probability is the highest on this slate. El Hadji Malick Diouf and Krepin Diatta as the two confirmed corner takers are the Senegal set-piece core. A Senegal win or draw scenario significantly changes the value of their attacking stack.

Algeria lost 3-0 to Argentina in Round 1 as the defending champions dominated. Despite conceding three goals, three attacking substitutions were made at 64 minutes including key creative players who now start here. Algeria must win this Round 2 matchup against Jordan to keep their tournament alive.

Amine Gouiri and Riyad Mahrez both lead the Algeria projection at 10.47 fpts in attack — Gouiri started Round 1 and was replaced at 64 minutes, while Mahrez entered that same minute as a substitute. Both now start here. Mahrez (confirmed corner kick taker, $4,800) and Fares Chaibi (10.26 fpts, $4,700) round out a deep Algeria attacking group.

Algeria project 1.86 goals against Jordan's 0.83. Rayan Ait-Nouri (9.11 fpts, 19.55% proj_own) in defense provides attacking width and is the second-highest owned Algeria player. Luca Zidane (7.81 fpts, 21.21% proj_own) in goal carries the highest goalkeeper ownership on this slate.

Algeria stack construction centers on Gouiri, Mahrez, and Chaibi in attack — all three project over 10 fpts. Ibrahim Maza (9.58 fpts, $5,700) provides a fourth viable attacking piece. Ait-Nouri at 19.55% proj_own in defense is the value anchor for any multi-game Algeria-heavy construction.

Jordan lost 3-1 to Austria in Round 1 — Ali Olwan scored in the 50th minute (assist Noor Al Rawabdeh) but conceded a 76th-minute own goal and an injury-time penalty. Salim Obaid and Saed Al-Rosan both entered in the final 20 minutes.

Mousa Al Tamari leads the Jordan projection at 9.27 fpts in attack as the confirmed corner kick taker at $4,900 with 21.21% proj_own — the highest-owned Jordan player. Ehsan Haddad (6.10 fpts, $4,300) and Odeh Fakhoury (5.72 fpts, $3,900) provide the supporting midfield output.

Jordan project 0.83 goals against Algeria's 1.86. At 15.78% implied win probability, Jordan plays are GPP-only. Yazeed Abulaila (4.16 fpts, 5.63% proj_own) in goal at $4,100 is the secondary Jordan ownership option after Al Tamari.

Jordan GPP plays center entirely on Al Tamari as the lone confirmed corner taker with viable projection. A repeat of their Round 1 goal — scored from a competitive game-script moment at 50 minutes — would be required to generate meaningful DFS output against Algeria.
